e-3634.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of the two functions $u(x)=x$ and $v(x)=\cos x .$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\eqalign{
	 (x\cos x)' &=   u'(x) \cdot v(x) + u(x) \cdot v'(x)\
						&= (x)'\cdot \cos x + x\cdot (\cos x)'\
					   & = 1 \cdot \cos x + x (-\sin x)\
					  & =  \cos x - x \sin x					

}
$$

e-3635.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Product Containing an Exponential or Logarithmic Function
e-3635.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x) = x^2$ and $v(x)=\ln x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={({x}^{2})}^{′}ln⁡x+{x}^{2}{(ln⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =2x\cdot ln⁡x+{x}^{2}(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =2xln⁡x+x \\  & =x(2ln⁡x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

e-3636.knowledge_point: Finding the Slope of the Tangent Line to a Product  at a Given Point
e-3636.problem: If a curve $\mathcal C$ is given by $y=e^x\sin x,$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=\dfrac \pi 2.$
e-3636.worked_solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x) = e^x$ and $v(x)=\sin{x}.$ Then, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = e^x,\qquad \dfrac{\textrm d v}{\textrm d x} = \cos x.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{x}\cdot cos⁡x+sin⁡x\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & ={e}^{x}(cos⁡x+sin⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\dfrac\pi 2$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=\pi /2} & ={e}^{\pi /2}(cos⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+sin⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & ={e}^{\pi /2}(0+1) \\  & ={e}^{\pi /2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $e^{\pi/2}.$

Differentiate excos⁡x.

a
−excos⁡x−exsin⁡x
b
excos⁡x−exsin⁡x
c
 excos⁡x+sin⁡x

excos⁡x+exsin⁡x

EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of the two functions u(x)=ex and v(x)=cos⁡x. So, we apply the product rule:

(excos⁡x)′=u′(x)⋅v(x)+u(x)⋅v′(x)=(ex)′⋅cos⁡x+ex⋅(cos⁡x)′=(ex)(cos⁡x)+(ex)(−sin⁡x)=excos⁡x−exsin⁡x

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms the product rule gives e^x cos x − e^x sin x, matching option b. The deliberately submitted option a has an incorrect negative sign on the first term.

content.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of the two functions $u(x)={e}^{x}$ and $v(x)=cos⁡x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}({e}^{x}cos⁡x)^{′} & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =({e}^{x})^{′}\cdot cos⁡x+{e}^{x}\cdot (cos⁡x)^{′} \\  & =({e}^{x})(cos⁡x)+({e}^{x})(-sin⁡x) \\  & ={e}^{x}cos⁡x-{e}^{x}sin⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 14
after.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y={e}^{x}sin⁡x,$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=\pi .$
after.worked_solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x)={e}^{x}$ and $v(x)=sin⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=cos⁡x.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{x}\cdot cos⁡x+(sin⁡x)\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & ={e}^{x}(cos⁡x+sin⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\pi $ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=\pi } & ={{e}^{x}(cos⁡x+sin⁡x)|}_{x=\pi } \\  & ={e}^{\pi }(-1+0) \\  & =-{e}^{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $-{e}^{\pi }.$

after.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y=(x+2)cos⁡x,$ then the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ is{{field-1}}.
after.worked_solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x)=x+2$ and $v(x)=cos⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1,\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=-sin⁡x.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =(x+2)\cdot (-sin⁡x)+cos⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & =-(x+2)sin⁡x+cos⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=\frac{\pi }{2}} & =-(\frac{\pi }{2}+2)sin⁡\frac{\pi }{2}+cos⁡\frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =-(\frac{\pi }{2}+2)(1)+0 \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{2}-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $-\frac{\pi }{2}-2.$
